articles.title: Explain This Thing: An AI That Helps My Parents Understand Their Devices
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend My parents often use household devices like the AC, microwave, TV, and dishwasher, but they sometimes forget what parti…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built My parents often use household devices like the AC, microwave, TV, and dishwasher, but they sometimes forget what particular buttons do. Usually, they would have to ask me: “What does this button do?” And because these devices have so many buttons and modes, remembering them isn't always easy. So I built Explain This Thing — a small personalized AI assistant that lets them upload a photo of a remote or control panel or used a saved photo, tap the button they're confused about, and get a simple explanation in English or Hindi. The goal wasn't to build an AI that understands every appliance in the world. I wanted to build something that understands the few devices my parents actually use.
articles.author: Muskan Khatoon

articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend I built LocalLens, a privacy-first, on-device AI browser extension (MV3) that turns natural language instructions into…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built I built LocalLens , a privacy-first, on-device AI browser extension (MV3) that turns natural language instructions into precise web browser actions—without sending raw page content, screenshots, or sensitive data to remote cloud servers. I built it specifically for my friend Ankit , who regularly interacts with online administrative dashboards, complex web portals, and local developer environments. Ankit wanted an intelligent web assistant to automate repetitive tasks like form auto-filling, table parsing, and navigating dense documentation panels.
articles.author: Yuvraj Sau

articles.title: Study Buddy: an offline GATE study partner for my friend, built with Ollama
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend Study Buddy is an offline exam study partner I built for my friend Anushka, who is preparing for GATE. GATE has a huge…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built Study Buddy is an offline exam study partner I built for my friend Anushka , who is preparing for GATE . GATE has a huge syllabus, and she wanted quick answers and practice questions from her own notes. I also wanted her study material to stay on her laptop and not go to someone else's server. You add your notes (PDF, text or markdown) to a folder, and Study Buddy does three things: Answers from your notes only. Every answer cites its source, like [notes.pdf p.3] . If the notes don't cover a question, it says so instead of guessing. Quizzes you on your own material. It writes multiple-choice questions from the notes and explains each answer with a pointer to the source. Tracks your weak spots.
articles.author: Khushighosh

articles.title: Horizon -Look Back & See Forward.
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend A journal is good at remembering what happened. But after months of writing, it becomes surprisingly difficult to remem…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built A journal is good at remembering what happened. But after months of writing, it becomes surprisingly difficult to remember what kept happening. I built Horizon , an intelligence layer on top of a personal journal. The journaling experience stays familiar, and the journal becomes more useful the longer you write in it. Instead of only asking: "What did I write?" you can ask: "What have I been repeatedly thinking about?" "What have I been putting off?" "What has been taking most of my attention lately?" Horizon answers using your own journal history, and every answer links back to the entries it came from.
articles.author: Harsh Srivastava

articles.body: First day on Bourbon Street, and my sister and I had the most important question of the trip: where are we going to eat? It should have been easy. Between the two of us, we had added sixty-eight restaurants, bars, cafés, and attractions to Le Voyage , a travel-planning app I vibecoded the better part of a year earlier. We were standing in the middle of the French Quarter, surrounded by food, carrying a small database of places we already wanted to try, and we were still hungry and indecisive. So we opened the app. Le Voyage started as something I built for a trip to Paris. The idea was simple.

articles.title: NudgeBox -- A privacy-first agent that reads a job seeker's Gmail, finds interviews and online assessments (OAs), and "nudges" them!
articles.excerpt: What I Built My friend Tushar is a brilliant developer, but his inbox is an absolute disaster zone. Last month, he got a recruiter screen invite for a job he really wanted, but because the recruiter u…
articles.body: What I Built The job market is brutal right now, but what's even worse is finally getting an interview and then completely missing it. My friend Tushar is a brilliant developer, but his inbox is an absolute disaster zone. Last month, he got a recruiter screen invite for a job he really wanted, but because the recruiter used a weird timezone abbreviation and it got buried under 50 marketing emails, he completely missed the call. He was devastated. So, I built NudgeBox for him. It's an autonomous AI exoskeleton that securely reads his inbox, identifies interviews and online assessments (OAs), and durably schedules aggressive nudges (T-7 days, T-1 day, morning-of, and T-1 hour) so he is always prepared.
articles.author: Chaitanya Yadav

articles.excerpt: WhatsApp Automation for Clinics: A Complete Implementation Guide How to automate appointment booking, reminders, and patient follow-up using the WhatsApp Business API — with full code examples. If you…
articles.body: WhatsApp Automation for Clinics: A Complete Implementation Guide How to automate appointment booking, reminders, and patient follow-up using the WhatsApp Business API — with full code examples. If you run a clinic in India, you know the daily grind: patients calling to book appointments, front-desk staff confirming slots, reminder calls the day before, and the dreaded no-shows that leave your schedule full of empty chairs. The average Indian clinic loses 20–30% of daily appointments to no-shows . For a clinic seeing 30 patients a day, that's 6–9 empty slots — revenue you can never recover. Add to that the hours your front desk spends on booking calls and status queries, and you're looking at a significant operational drain. WhatsApp automation fixes this.

articles.title: 8 Video Game Villains With Motives You Can't Argue With

articles.body: Grab your gavel: Court is in session for eight of gaming’s most misunderstood villains. Their charges? One occupied planet, one erased painting, one underwater utopia gone to rot, and a truly staggering body count. But, all that aside, what if these bad guys were actually making a somewhat decent point? Read between the lines of their melodramatic monologues, and perhaps you’ll realize that, say, a centuries-long guilt trip over one catastrophic mistake was in fact understandable rationale for wanting to tear the world down and start over. Or not: You get to decide. Just read each villain’s case file below before reaching a verdict — you might not love where the evidence actually points.

articles.excerpt: Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office.
articles.body: Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office. It's a crushing start for the Alejandro González Iñárritu-directed dark comedy. The movie, which stars an unrecognizable Cruise under a thick bed of makeup, accumulated just $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally. It's a $20 million total that props Digger up to be crushed under the weight of its $160 million production budget (via Deadline ). With marketing costs unclear, it signals a long, long line to walk if the movie wants to even sniff at turning a profit. "An oil tycoon faces a mounting environmental catastrophe as politicians and scientists struggle to contain the crisis," a description for Digger says.

In a week full of calls, meetings, and classes, most of them are gone by the time you need them. A standard voice recorder certainly helps, but it leaves you with hours of audio and transcripts to dig through, with nothing linking the words to the files, photos, and earlier conversations around them. The Soulog Sense , paired with the Soulog app, not only records and transcribes the conversation but also sorts it by topic and decision and connects it to the surrounding material, so you can search it, revisit it, and build on it later. articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 3 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Selfie at Vera Rubin Ridge Explanation: On sol 1943 of its journey of exploration across the surface of Mars, the Curiosity Rover recorded this selfie at the south rim of Vera Rubin Ridge. Of course a sol is a Martian solar day , about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day. Curiosity’s sol 1943 corresponds to Earth date January 23, 2018.

articles.excerpt: As part of NASA’s ongoing Inspiration Tour, NASA astronaut Christina Koch will highlight America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation at the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Los Angeles…
articles.body: NASA astronaut Christina Koch is seen during an event to award the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the Artemis II crew, Friday, Aug. 28, 2026, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/John Kraus As part of NASA’s ongoing Inspiration Tour, NASA astronaut Christina Koch will highlight America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation at the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Los Angeles Rams game in Philadelphia on Sunday, Oct. 4. A self-proclaimed Philadelphia sports fan, Koch is an explorer and engineer who spent a total of 338 days in space across two missions, including serving as a mission specialist for the agency’s Artemis II mission earlier this year.

articles.title: Heading Home: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Concludes Station Science Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Ro…
articles.body: 5 Min Read Heading Home: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Concludes Station Science Mission NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will head home from the International Space Station after supporting research that benefits life on Earth and prepares humans for missions into deep space. Here’s a look back at some of their accomplishments: Orbital transit NASA/ESA The crew members look out the window of a Dragon spacecraft during their journey to the space station, a destination that offers a unique vantage point to observe both Earth and the cosmos.
